biography.plain_text: Konstantin Zasov is a Russian transport entrepreneur who co-founded Rustranscom with Konstantin Sintsov, building an owned railway group around grain, fertiliser and timber freight. A former Rusagrotrans chief executive, he developed the business through fleet investment and acquisitions before its sale to Demetra Holding. He previously worked in the railway equipment industry.

long_biography.plain_text:
As president of Rustranscom, Konstantin Zasov focused on using existing freight wagons more efficiently. Fertiliser producers often kept their own fleets to guarantee deliveries, even when vehicles were poorly positioned for other work. His group offered to manage those wagons while guaranteeing the owners transport capacity, reallocating equipment to more effective routes.

He also sought to simplify how grain customers booked transport. Rustranscom worked with the Moscow Exchange so its logistics service could be sold alongside grain futures. Zasov wanted electronic paperwork and coordinated port movements to reduce long booking delays.

uncertainties: Research current to 1 October 2026. Identity confidence is bounded at 81: exact uncommon name and Russian business identity have contextual maritime corroboration, but no independent document ties the person to the specific Far Away or Oceanic 143 hulls. The mirrored company began later and cannot establish earlier boat ownership.

Do not conflate Zasov with partner Konstantin Sintsov or import the partner's education, hometown, sports achievements or charity. Karting entry lists containing this name do not establish the same individual or support family facts, nationality changes or sporting tags.

Public descriptions variously date the early business, operating subsidiary and group consolidation. Biographies avoid a single misleading formation year. The proposed public share offering did not become proof of a completed listing.

Completed August 2021 consolidation and a newly appointed president supersede older retained-share and current-president descriptions. A contemporaneous Demetra board seat is not current personal ownership; the new owner company's state-linked assets are not attributed to him.

The 2021 securities filing proves a separate investment vehicle but supplies no current full portfolio or principal mandate. Its professional adviser is owned by another person. Finance and passive ownership were tested and not forced from one dated holding.

Railway formation involved leased public rolling stock and later corporate purchases. Beneficial equity is separately evidenced; neither the state fleet nor the group's managed client assets are treated as entirely his private property.

All relevant personal profiles were searched in English and Russian: Forbes, Wikipedia, Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook, Twitter/X, Youtube, TikTok and Personal Website. No reliable personal account emerged. Search hits included the partner and unrelated sporting records; TikTok was inaccessible. The historical operating-company site failed to load and is not proposed as a verified link.

Birth year, patronymic and city have direct contemporary biographical support. Exact day and month, secondary nationality and current residence were not independently established. Existing mortality Unknown is preserved because the strongest direct personal statements are historical; no inference of death is made.

The minimum approved active Freight rail tag captures the defining owned activity. Agriculture, fertilisers, forestry, securities investment and manufacturing tags would confuse customers, isolated investments or earlier employment with separately demonstrated specialisms.

Published biographies exclude anonymous allegations, political speculation and private family information. All final material relies on complete relevant source bodies; mirror data is used only with explicit provenance and limited weight.

Source word budgets include prose, brief and metadata. The 2018 interview supplies the long operating details within 200 derived words; the distinct 2012 interview supplies financing context. Reproductions count as one source, not additional independent corroboration.
